title: Electric field along y
spoken: The moving electric field along y is gamma times E y minus v B z.
explanation: With no electric field and a magnetic field along positive z, an observer moving along positive x finds an electric field along negative y: the force on a moving charge becomes, in its own system, an electric force.
assumptions: The moving system moves along x at speed v relative to the stationary system, with |v| < c. Modern teaching notation: gamma is the paper's beta, c its V.
Fields in empty space, in SI units; E is the electric field and B the magnetic field, with components along x, y and z.

notes.title: The two together
notes.explanation: In the moving system, what was a pure magnetic field is partly electric, and the other way round.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: Electric and magnetic fields are not separately the same in both systems; their components across the motion mix.

notes.title: Times gamma
notes.explanation: The same factor as for coordinates.

notes.title: Speed times the other field
notes.explanation: The other field, carried past at speed v, contributes to this one.

notes.title: Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: One over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared. At 0.6c it is 1.25.

notes.title: Electric field, moving system
notes.explanation: The electric field in the moving system, one component; the subscript names which.

notes.title: Magnetic field, stationary system
notes.explanation: The magnetic field in the stationary system, one component; the subscript names which.

notes.title: Electric field, stationary system
notes.explanation: The electric field in the stationary system, one component; the subscript names which.

notes.title: Speed of the moving system
notes.explanation: Along x. Its sign gives the direction.
